scientific_question: After animal and plant taxa are prospectively matched on observation architecture within region, is the held-out recovery lift of the frozen ACSP robust-support method larger for animals than plants?

acsp_method.comparator: same candidate universe and same selected-cell count
acsp_method.failed_or_empty_fold_rule: recall=0, random_mean_recall=0, lift=0; retain in denominator

biological_replication.unit: prospectively matched animal-plant taxon pair within the same Japanese region
biological_replication.pair_value: mean over five declared spatial folds of robust lift over same-size random

primary_estimand.name: animal_minus_plant_matched_pair_lift
primary_estimand.per_pair: animal pair-mean lift minus matched plant pair-mean lift
primary_estimand.overall: unweighted mean over all 24 matched pairs

primary_inference.exact_sign_flip: enumerate all 2^24 sign assignments to the 24 paired differences
primary_inference.support_rule: exact one-sided sign-flip p < 0.05 AND matched-pair bootstrap 95% CI lower bound > 0

secondary_descriptive: mean selected cells and patch count by group
claim_if_supported: Within this fresh observation-balanced Japanese cohort, animals show greater robust-support held-out recovery enrichment than matched plants under the frozen ACSP method.
claim_if_not_supported: The historical animal-greater-than-plant lift contrast does not reproduce after observation architecture is balanced prospectively; do not interpret the original subgroup difference as a taxonomic ecological effect.
prohibited: claim universal animal versus plant difference
interpret difference as dispersal mechanism without trait analysis
replace taxa or matched pairs after recovery outcomes
change support fraction, patch distance, recovery radius, random comparator or pair weighting after outcome
treat 240 folds as independent biological replicates
use post-outcome IPW to rescue a failed matched design
